Who's playing

Co-op · Original monsters · Normal · Up to 8 players

Start a game with Esc → Single Player → New Game. Use the in-game menus to change controls, difficulty, video, sound, and saves. Mouse capture and audio require a click.

On a phone or tablet, Touch controls turn on by themselves: drag on the left to move (push further to run), drag on the right or on Fire to look, and use Menu for the game menus. The game's Mouse Speed option also sets how fast the view turns.

Music: checking…. Name files like track02.ogg to track11.ogg, matching the original CD tracks. Your files stay in this browser and are used before any music on the server. Change the volume in Options → Music Volume.

The installed data contains the first episode. Select pak0.pak and pak1.pak from your purchased copy before launching to play the full campaign. Files you select stay on your computer.

The original shareware is available as a complete, unchanged archive. Its original license accompanies the game data.

Click Join co-op to fight Quake's original monsters together on the shared server. Up to eight players share the campaign, enemies, and level progress. Other players can open this page and join the same game. Use Quake's console to chat with say hello. Single-player saves remain available after leaving multiplayer.

Select Deathmatch, then click Join deathmatch for player-versus-player combat in a separate eight-player room. There are no monsters. Use the original weapons and pickups, hold Tab for frag scores, and press fire after dying to respawn. A round ends at 20 frags or 10 minutes; press fire after intermission to start the next round. Switching modes moves only you; co-op continues for its other players.

Multiplayer uses WebTransport.

This build runs QuakeSpasm through WebAssembly and GL4ES. The shareware data has no soundtrack; add your own above.
